subject: Post-call: deployment path & compliance evidence for SynapseCare
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@synapsecare.com>, procurement@synapsecare.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: deployment path & compliance evidence for SynapseCare

Hi Olivia — great to meet you and the SynapseCare team on today's call. Quick recap and clear next steps so we're aligned on hosting options and evidence you'll need to move to procurement: 

Summary of ask
- Primary constraint: HIPAA-covered workflows processing PHI (E/M notes + patient messaging).
- Preference stated on call: Private VPC or on-prem if procurement requires full network isolation; open to Dedicated if private proves cost-prohibitive.
- Procurement will require a BAA + SOC 2 artifacts and an inventory of audit evidence (logs, retention, access controls).

What Redwood can provide
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live, no BAA by default for PHI workloads (not recommended for PHI).
- Dedicated capacity: isolated GPU pools, BAA available, expected predictable throughput, lower setup cycle (2-4 weeks post-contract).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): BAA + on-prem options, KMS/HSM integrations, full audit logging, and network isolation; longer procurement and onboarding timeline (6–10 weeks).

Immediate next steps (action owners)
1) Logan — share SOC 2 summary, BAA template, and a short checklist of evidence items (attached). Target: today.
2) Olivia — confirm whether procurement needs on-prem (air-gapped) or VPC (customer-managed VPC). Reply with preference and any vendor security questionnaire. Target: EOD 2026-12-01.
3) Rishi/Marissa — if SynapseCare prefers Private, prepare a pricing delta and onboarding timeline for Dedicated vs Private options. Target: 2026-12-02.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (summary), redwood_baa_template.pdf (template) — both attached to this thread.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute procurement & security sync on 2026-12-03 or 2026-12-06. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0164

From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@synapsecare.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:37:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment path & compliance evidence for SynapseCare

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear recap. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement/security as we start our internal review: 

1) BAA scope: will Redwood sign a standard BAA covering processing and subprocessing? If yes, are there known carve-outs for telemetry/metadata?
2) SOC 2: can you provide the specific date of your last Type II report and a short list of artifacts we can expect (log retention windows, authentication model, incident response runbook excerpts)?
3) Private vs Dedicated cost: we need a ballpark monthly delta (order-of-magnitude) to include in our TCO for the board. Dedicated sounds like a reasonable compromise if private is 3–4x the cost. Can you confirm typical ranges?
4) Network isolation: for Private VPC — do you support customer-managed routing/peering and HSM integration for key custody?

Also attaching our vendor security questionnaire (VSAQ_ SynapseCare_Procurement.xlsx). If you could flag rows that will need engineering input, that would help.

We are leaning toward Private VPC, but procurement asked to validate whether Dedicated + BAA with strict logging could be an acceptable stopgap to accelerate go-live.

Best,
Olivia Grant
Head of Clinical Ops
SynapseCare
olivia.grant@synapsecare.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment path & compliance evidence for SynapseCare

Hi Olivia — answers inline and materials attached. Thanks for the questionnaire — we'll flag engineering items in a separate pass.

1) BAA: Yes, Redwood will sign a standard BAA that covers processing and subprocessors. Typical carve-outs are limited to anonymized telemetry; anything that could contain PHI is scoped into the BAA. We can walk through contract language if legal wants to redline.

2) SOC 2: Last Type II report period: Jan 1, 2026 – Jun 30, 2026. Attach: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (redwood can share redacted Type II under NDA). Expected artifacts we can provide quickly:
- System logs (7–90 day windows configurable, full audit logs on Private)
- Authentication: SSO + optional SAML/OIDC, MFA enforced for console
- IR runbook excerpts + contact for incident response

3) Cost delta (ballpark monthly):
- Dedicated: base committed pool starts ~$28k/month for a mid-sized production pool (predictable throughput, BAA available).
- Private VPC (customer-managed): typically 1.8–2.6x Dedicated depending on network egress and on-request isolation (this includes engineering onboarding and baseline HSM/KMS integration).
- On-prem: can be materially higher; depends on customer infra and support SLA (usually a one-time onboarding + ongoing support retainer).

I'll attach a short cost-estimate workbook (private-vpc-cost-estimate.xlsx) with example line items. These are order-of-magnitude numbers — Rishi will build a formal quote if you confirm preferred path.

4) Network isolation: Yes — Private supports customer-managed VPC peering, private peering, and HSM/KMS integrations (we have partners for common HSMs). We can provide a wiring diagram and gating checklist for peering and routing.

Proposed immediate next step: can we schedule a 30-minute technical sync where Rishi (security/solutions) walks through the VPC + HSM checklist and Marissa (onboarding lead) reviews timelines? 2026-12-03 09:00 PT or 2026-12-06 11:00 PT both work for us.

I'll also flag the VSAQ rows that need engineering input and return that by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
